findings.location: A-9 (agt-4p2.9) design and acceptance criteria: schema-mismatch resends
findings.what_changed: Schema-mismatch resends got a fresh send count and a fresh 90 s budget: decoded replies were counted apart from the busy and timeout sends of each reply (an assistant decision), with `attempts: Attempts, // fresh after each schema resend`, and the AC said "decision.schema_mismatch ... after max_sends decoded replies". One request could be sent max_sends x max_sends times (25 by default), and the 90 s attempt budget restarted after each schema resend. owner-llm-decider-mode leaves the mechanism to the assistant, but not the cap. Reviewer rating: medium; owner call.

authority.quote: resent unchanged, up to the configured maximum number of sends

findings.suggested_fix: Keep one send counter and one budget per request, shared by busy, timeout and schema-mismatch resends; or get the owner to approve the per-reply count explicitly. Also contradicts owner-busy-resend ("Max sends configurable, default 5 ... 90 s attempt budget").
findings.fix_note: Busy, timeout and schema resends share one max_sends and one 90 s budget per request (REQ-SAG-0901). Gate re-run: pass.

findings.what_changed: The line "sc-decision-llm and sc-llm-provider import every Jev-mapped type (SystemOneRequest, SystemOneResponse and the answer types) from sc-decision-schema" made sc-llm-provider depend on the decision schema. The same sprint's ADR-SAG-0004 AC says sc-llm-provider's only sc-agent dependencies are types, secrets, log and http, and A-7 design line 232 says "sc-decision-schema does not depend on either". Reviewer rating: low; wording fix.

authority.quote: let a non-decision program use HTTP, providers and logging without decision types

findings.suggested_fix: "sc-decision-llm imports every Jev-mapped type from sc-decision-schema and defines none of its own; sc-llm-provider defines and uses no Jev-mapped type." Also contradicts owner-architecture ("sc-llm-provider -> sc-decision-llm").
findings.fix_note: Only sc-decision-llm imports Jev types; sc-llm-provider uses no decision types (ADR-SAG-0004). Gate re-run: pass.

findings.what_changed: ANC-004 was retired as "covered by REQ-SAG-0008 (optional logger injection with default loggers)", but REQ-SAG-0008 covers injection and defaults only; the other half of the owner's words had no anchor or requirement. The sprints that log are A-5 (http), A-8, A-9 and A-10; A-4 and A-6 had no general-log events of their own, and A-6 discovery was logged only through HttpClient. Mitigation: ANC-004 was only proposed, never locked, so it is not among the 11 approved anchors. Reviewer rating: low.

authority.quote: You need to go through the code and add logging and inject the logger everywhere that should have had it from day-1.

findings.suggested_fix: Re-propose a narrowed anchor, e.g. "every sc-agent library crate that performs I/O logs through the injected or default general logger"; or record that the owner accepts REQ-SAG-0008 as sufficient.
findings.fix_note: New anchor ANC-007, locked: "The existing sc-agent library code must be updated so that it writes log records." The statement drops "inject the logger" (REQ-SAG-0008 covers injection) and "everywhere"; about 70 wordings that kept both failed the rubric (faithful or single_constraint). Rubric 3/3 pass; fixtures pass; tuned questions 54/54 cells (default questions 46/54, 2 unstable cases). Sprint lines added: A-6 (availability-check records), A-7 (request, token usage, schema mismatch), A-9 (stream start/end, worker stop, session-log failure), A-10 (send, models, doctor; sc-agent-py accepts a logger). Excluded: A-1 (types only, below the log layer), A-2 (ANC-001 bars logging code), A-3 (sc-treesitter depends on no sc-agent crate; tsq logging is in A-10), A-4 (ADR-SAG-0004: config and secrets share sc-agent-log's layer and may depend only on lower layers, so their callers log key source and config events).

acceptable_choices.note: On an equal release date the config model wins (owner said he does not care). A-10 doctor warns on equal dates, as REQ-SAG-0503 requires.
Provider::PRIORITY = TypeSafe, Anthropic, OpenAi, OpenRouter, Together, Nous (direct providers before aggregators; assistant decision).
jev-1.13.0's release date is a TODO for the owner. docs.typesafe.ai gives none, and the sprint cannot close without it. Owner said "look it up"; it was looked up and not found.
New crate crates/sc-treesitter-py; 19 error variants (the owner's 17 plus Write and Log, added for tsq).
tsq lives in sc-treesitter behind a default `cli` feature (clap and sc-observability). The "library writes no log" check therefore runs with --no-default-features.
Deps keyring and whoami; config file ~/.sc-agent/default.json with SC_AGENT__ env overrides; a runner named like a short name is rejected (config.runner_name).
Retry-After counts as valid only when it is 1-32 ASCII digits with an optional fraction; after 8 s the backoff keeps doubling, capped at 30 s.
Daemon kinds are strands, laya, mapika and generic (`decider` renamed `strands` to keep it apart from Mapika/decider); a 503 from a local daemon is final.
sc-llm-provider "sits on the http layer". This is stricter than the anchor's "decision backends (sc-decision-llm over sc-llm-provider)" and matches the ADR rationale.
The decider system prompt is drafted by the assistant for owner review (Mapika/decider uses none).
Invented test name log_error_keeps_lower_layer_cause (harmless).
Default log_root is ~/.sc-agent, which matches sc-observability's documented default `~/.<app>` (checked in its docs).
Queue capacity is a constant 4 x workers, not a config key.
A single `decide` holds off on the caller's thread with CancelToken::wait_until rather than in the queue. Idle workers use Condvar timed waits. Neither is a sleep.
New crates `decide` (lib + bin) and `sc-agent-py` (module sc_agent, publish=false, depends on the decide lib).
This is not scope creep. REQ-SAG-0002, 0004, 0007 and REQ-SAG-0104 AC2 already require PyO3 bindings, and no earlier sprint delivered them.
`SagError` is a Python exception carrying (id, message, detail chain), the same pattern as TreesitterError in A-3. It is consistent with the per-crate error unions.
--project and --agent-role are required with no default; tsq logs to the fixed path ~/.sc-agent/logs/tsq.log.jsonl, because sc-treesitter may not read sc-agent-config.

ANC-003 ("no REQ/NFR/ADR/bead cites plan-anchor or judge-jev as a source") is still only proposed and gated nowhere. The designs mention plan-anchor and judge-jev only as agent_role examples and in REQ-SAG-0006 text.
